547ba1e2-847f-4993-ab69-4c357dd58551.Title: AWS IAM
547ba1e2-847f-4993-ab69-4c357dd58551.Note: Identity and access management. Controls who can do what across all AWS services via users, roles, and policies. Every service depends on IAM for permissions.

99423588-8e7f-40b8-a684-73400d8fb7d5.Title: AWS S3
99423588-8e7f-40b8-a684-73400d8fb7d5.Note: Object storage. Acts as the central data lake — stores raw files (CSV, JSON, Parquet, ORC) that other services read from and write to. Supports lifecycle rules, versioning, encryption, and event notifications.

958b9c16-d7ed-44a7-84ff-630d116a4f2e.Title: VPC
958b9c16-d7ed-44a7-84ff-630d116a4f2e.Note:
Virtual Private Cloud. Isolated network for AWS resources. Services like EMR, Redshift, and RDS run inside VPCs. Misconfigurations (missing endpoints, wrong security groups) are common exam traps. Contains public and private subnets in which you can define to allow for access scopes.

Has an internal framework of CIDR Blocks, that allow you to launch various non-regional AWS services available to other services or allow for public access. However, you can define private endpoints via VPC to allow for regional instances to communicate with other instances without having to go through the public web (www.)\

A default VPC for each AWS region is automatically created for each account, allowing for users to instantly launch EC2 instances, Load Balancers, RDS databases, etc.

19941086-d024-4db7-89a8-66d1c560dece.Title: CloudWatch
19941086-d024-4db7-89a8-66d1c560dece.Note: Monitoring and observability. Collects logs, metrics, and alarms for all services. Used to troubleshoot pipeline failures, set alerts, and query logs via Logs Insights.

2862063f-ba2e-47d3-ba16-585b85714ab1.Title: CloudTrail
2862063f-ba2e-47d3-ba16-585b85714ab1.Note: API audit logging. Records every AWS API call (who did what, when). Delivers logs to S3 for compliance and can be queried via Athena for security analysis.

9349b634-1a2b-46c5-8f10-2f564c346154.Title: Lambda
9349b634-1a2b-46c5-8f10-2f564c346154.Note: Serverless compute. Runs code in response to events (S3 uploads, Kinesis records, DynamoDB changes). The glue for event-driven ETL. 15-min max runtime, 10GB memory limit.

1f90fddf-ae56-4bd6-8389-f773d07efe3f.Title: EC2
1f90fddf-ae56-4bd6-8389-f773d07efe3f.Note: Virtual machines. Foundation for EMR clusters and self-managed workloads. Key concepts: instance types (compute/memory/storage optimized), Spot vs On-Demand pricing, instance profiles for IAM roles.

47da2804-5632-4f33-aeb9-50ce6a3edf77.Title: AWS Glue
47da2804-5632-4f33-aeb9-50ce6a3edf77.Note: Managed serverless ETL service. Runs Apache Spark jobs to extract, transform, and load data. Handles schema inference, job bookmarks (tracks processed data), and auto-generates ETL scripts.

198bf9bc-61c3-45bd-acaa-521db5b3936c.Title: Data Catalog
198bf9bc-61c3-45bd-acaa-521db5b3936c.Note: Centralized metadata store (part of Glue). Crawlers scan S3/databases and infer table schemas. Acts as the shared schema layer for Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR — they all query through it.

16d6ebf6-f57a-469d-9eba-57b13c968f07.Title: Athena
16d6ebf6-f57a-469d-9eba-57b13c968f07.Note: Serverless SQL query engine over S3. Uses schemas from Data Catalog. Pay per TB scanned. Optimized by using Parquet/ORC, partitioning, and predicate pushdown. Best for ad-hoc and infrequent queries.

aff9422e-4694-4c7f-88c3-e4177fc2985d.Title: Redshift
aff9422e-4694-4c7f-88c3-e4177fc2985d.Note: Managed data warehouse for heavy analytical workloads. Data is loaded INTO Redshift storage. Supports complex joins, aggregations, and materialized views. Redshift Spectrum extends queries to S3 without loading data.

0c623b5b-0a4a-456a-b03c-c5f715a76296.Title: Kinesis Data Streams
0c623b5b-0a4a-456a-b03c-c5f715a76296.Note: Real-time data streaming. You manage shards and write custom consumers (Lambda, KCL apps). Sub-second latency. Use when you need fine-grained control over stream processing and or retries.

ce55a90e-9e60-4a37-b80e-0822c7f53824.Title: Kinesis Data Firehose
ce55a90e-9e60-4a37-b80e-0822c7f53824.Note: Managed near-real-time delivery pipe. Auto-batches, compresses, and delivers data to S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, or Splunk. No shards to manage. Minimum 60-second buffer. Can transform in-flight via Lambda.

919b792f-fede-4aab-b080-f4c95ac6f269.Title: EMR
919b792f-fede-4aab-b080-f4c95ac6f269.Note: Managed clusters for big data frameworks (Spark, Hive, Presto, Flink). Runs on EC2 or EKS. Use for terabyte-scale ETL, ML feature engineering, and processing too heavy for Athena/Lambda. Exam loves Spot instances for cost optimization.

4751feaf-235f-4e9a-8c04-1f3d1fa18dd9.Title: MSK
4751feaf-235f-4e9a-8c04-1f3d1fa18dd9.Note: Managed Apache Kafka. Fully managed Kafka clusters for high-throughput event streaming. Use over Kinesis when you need Kafka-native APIs, higher retention, or existing Kafka ecosystem tooling.

b58ba90a-529e-4bd5-9c3c-ee52ee83bc2a.Title: Lake Formation
b58ba90a-529e-4bd5-9c3c-ee52ee83bc2a.Note: Data lake governance layer on top of Glue Data Catalog. Manages fine-grained access control (column/row-level), data sharing across accounts, and centralized permissions. Not an ETL or query engine itself.

fcb04d24-2a77-4d0f-bc19-f53a7fdeed08.Title: Step Functions
fcb04d24-2a77-4d0f-bc19-f53a7fdeed08.Note: Serverless workflow orchestrator. Chains services (Lambda, Glue, EMR, ECS) into state machines with branching, retries, and error handling. Use for multi-step ETL pipelines. Standard (long-running) vs Express (high-volume, short) workflows.

b13ff62c-60d9-4c7c-bc3c-8a11571ad085.Title: EventBridge
b13ff62c-60d9-4c7c-bc3c-8a11571ad085.Note: Serverless event bus. Routes events between AWS services and custom apps using rules and patterns. Replaces CloudWatch Events. Use for scheduling (cron), reacting to state changes, and decoupling pipeline triggers.

bdd764bf-62ee-447b-b4ca-4121a1ef86e4.Title: SQS
bdd764bf-62ee-447b-b4ca-4121a1ef86e4.Note: Managed message queue. Decouples producers and consumers. Standard (at-least-once, unordered) vs FIFO (exactly-once, ordered). Use for buffering between pipeline stages. Dead letter queues catch failed messages.

94534ce5-9cc9-485a-a48d-ac4c4c75b788.Title: SNS
94534ce5-9cc9-485a-a48d-ac4c4c75b788.Note: Pub/sub messaging. One message fans out to multiple subscribers (SQS queues, Lambda, email, HTTP). Use for notifications (pipeline success/failure alerts) and fan-out patterns where one event triggers multiple consumers.

2b78bad5-d919-42f5-9780-dad37ddc0374.Title: DynamoDB
2b78bad5-d919-42f5-9780-dad37ddc0374.Note: Serverless NoSQL key-value/document database. Millisecond latency at any scale. Key concepts: partition key design, GSI/LSI, provisioned vs on-demand capacity, DynamoDB Streams for change data capture → Lambda.

3e0cccf0-5dcf-48ee-9bb5-a9ea22461731.Title: DMS
3e0cccf0-5dcf-48ee-9bb5-a9ea22461731.Note: Database Migration Service. Migrates data between databases (on-prem to cloud, RDS to Redshift, etc.). Supports one-time migration and ongoing replication (CDC — change data capture). Handles heterogeneous migrations (Oracle → Aurora).

b702a519-3477-41ad-bf10-9a5494bea680.Title: QuickSight
b702a519-3477-41ad-bf10-9a5494bea680.Note: Managed BI/visualization tool. Connects to Athena, Redshift, S3, RDS and generates dashboards, charts, and reports. SPICE is its in-memory engine for fast visualizations. The 'last mile' of the data pipeline.

0b0b58d2-878c-479b-84b4-6a32d0590425.Title: CloudFormation
0b0b58d2-878c-479b-84b4-6a32d0590425.Note: Infrastructure as Code. Defines AWS resources declaratively in JSON/YAML templates. Exam expects you to read templates and trace resource dependencies, not necessarily author from scratch. Essentially automates infrastructure as code by helping define steps to set up infrastructure, what services to set up, etc., so to avoid manually processes that might be prone to human error and also copy the steps as templates to be reused again. Using YAML and JSON, you configure, create, update, and or delete "stacks" (AWS Compute Resources).

b803d5b1-1147-425c-b36c-af170fc5b800.Title: KMS
b803d5b1-1147-425c-b36c-af170fc5b800.Note: Key Management Service. Creates and manages encryption keys. Used by S3 (SSE-KMS), Redshift, RDS, Kinesis, and Glue for data encryption at rest. Understand key policies, key rotation, and cross-account key access.

030b4a36-a818-45a1-b92f-f312190339ad.Title: CloudWatch Container Insights
030b4a36-a818-45a1-b92f-f312190339ad.Note: A subset of CloudWatch in which handles logging for multiple containerized applications (via EKS).

bd515be5-989d-4a7c-b0d4-8bbd05e5a3a1.Title: EFS
bd515be5-989d-4a7c-b0d4-8bbd05e5a3a1.Note: Elastic File Sharing service. Provides scalable file storage for EC2 or lambda instances, allowing them to be mounted on giving built-in File IO and mutability.

4ccb6b2f-2c7d-4e35-9ac3-66fddf2830ea.Title: DataBrew
4ccb6b2f-2c7d-4e35-9ac3-66fddf2830ea.Note: A no-code-low-code ETL service similar to regular Glue Jobs. Can do simple drag-drop flows for data cleaning and transformation, but lacks complexity when compared to Glue Jobs

b5d4af10-d9a8-4841-9e34-7793c1223a30.Title: RDS
b5d4af10-d9a8-4841-9e34-7793c1223a30.Note: Managed relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, etc.). Aurora is AWS-optimized with better performance and scaling. Key concepts: read replicas, Multi-AZ failover, RDS Proxy for Lambda connections, snapshot export to S3 as Parquet.

b6829d51-2415-4bf8-88bc-f476a36ec5e9.Title: RDS Aurora
b6829d51-2415-4bf8-88bc-f476a36ec5e9.Note: A subset of RDS in which is Amazon's custom SQL that is higher in availability and performance. An RDS can use different types of SQL engines like PostgreSQL and MySQL, but Amazon boasts of Aurora's capabilities at a higher cost per hour.

a751906d-07b4-4270-9a5c-0c9d0b5042bf.Title: Secrets Manager
a751906d-07b4-4270-9a5c-0c9d0b5042bf.Note: A subset of KMS in which allows for the creation, storage, and rotation of keys and secrets. The biggest feature is that it can conduct AUTOMATIC rotations of keys and secrets.

87f7a3be-6eeb-486e-84ee-4b0635891a5d.Title: API Gateway
87f7a3be-6eeb-486e-84ee-4b0635891a5d.Note: The routing service for incoming API requests. This service is the router in which directs requests to the correct backend. Often is used by Lambda as the front door!

44e04f58-d796-4cad-b552-9ec22eac07d7.Title: Glue Crawler
44e04f58-d796-4cad-b552-9ec22eac07d7.Note: Given a data source, scans the data within a infers a schema that is saved into the Data Catalog. Best used for scheduling crawl jobs so schema stays up to date and can conduct partition detection.

22610261-889d-4055-80a9-f7f7d56aa466.Title: Schema Registry
22610261-889d-4055-80a9-f7f7d56aa466.Note: Enforces and manages schema for streamed data. Can allow for versioning, but the core part of this service is that it validates incoming data within a constant data stream before it is processed.

90b0ac8d-2802-4241-8719-66a076dc7854.Title: Data Lake
90b0ac8d-2802-4241-8719-66a076dc7854.Note: A storage of unorganized and unstructured data that can be of multiple different formats. This is typically within object storage services like S3 or a general folder which houses a variety of files. Data here is always UNSTRUCTURED and UNPROCESSED.

9492b0fc-2599-44cc-a40b-80ebb4e2509b.Title: Data Warehouse
9492b0fc-2599-44cc-a40b-80ebb4e2509b.Note: A centralized database that contains CLEANED and PROCESSED data that is optimized for analytical queries. This can be a database that is an aggregation of multiple different data sources, or just a database of a cleaned data lake.

8abe5d13-8453-4838-bc66-954895e65f8f.Title: Internet Gateway
8abe5d13-8453-4838-bc66-954895e65f8f.Note: Allows instances to connect to the public internet.

a841e48d-1910-48f4-a4a2-38b71c5e55c7.Title: Customer Gateway
a841e48d-1910-48f4-a4a2-38b71c5e55c7.Note: Configured and established connection between VPCs and a third party on premise data center

8d1cdb43-cac8-4a4a-9cbc-a4fd93c2a332.Title: Carrier Gateways
8d1cdb43-cac8-4a4a-9cbc-a4fd93c2a332.Note: Allows for incoming traffic from a carrier network in a specific location

0f1d5963-63bb-42ae-b29e-fa4b8d7a6385.Title: Egress-only Internet Gateway
0f1d5963-63bb-42ae-b29e-fa4b8d7a6385.Note: Horizontally scaled and redundant VPC component that allows for outbound communication over IPv6 to public internet.
